snippet.title: Grinding Is Making You Worse. Here’s What the Best Do Instead.
snippet.description:
Get my free newsletter, The Pink Report: https://danielpink.substack.com/

We've become obsessed with discipline, intensity, and grinding. Those things matter, but after 25 years of studying human performance, I think we've got the formula at least half wrong. In this video, I'll show you why the best performers play instead of just grind, with help from two Nobel Prize-winning physicists, a study of 26,000 careers, and an Olympic champion who said she didn't need the gold medal right before she won it. Then I'll give you five ways to put it into practice this week.

In the video, I mention being loose vs. being tight. For a more comprehensive view of how tight and loose cultures shape every aspect of our lives, check out the brilliant book Rule Makers, Rule Breakers: How Tight and Loose Cultures Wire Our World by Michele Gelfand. It's seriously one of the most enlightening books I've ever read.

Here's the book: https://www.michelegelfand.com/rule-makers-rule-breakers

--

snippet.title: Can't Focus? Watch This Before You Sit Down to Work.
snippet.description:
Grab the free flow cheat sheet here: https://danpink.com/flow

When we sit down to do great work,  we often walk away having done only a fraction of it. Then we blame ourselves — our discipline, our willpower, our "focus."  

That's a mistake -- and it's holding us back. 

I've spent nearly 30 years studying motivation and human performance, and if there's one state that separates the work I'm proud of from the work I just grind through, it's flow — those stretches where time disappears and the work almost pulls itself out of you. Here's the good news: flow isn't magic. It's mechanics. And mechanics can be learned.

In this video I'll walk you through the exact system I use to drop into flow on demand — the same approach that's behind all seven of my books. No tricks, no hustle-culture nonsense. Just a handful of moves you can run every single day.

Fair warning: this one asks something of you. Watch it the way it's meant to be watched — full screen, phone away, one tab open. Think of it as your first rep.

snippet.title: How the Most Creative People Get Their Breakthroughs (It Isn't Hard Work)
snippet.description:
In this video, I'm tackling a question that's been bugging me for years: why do your best ideas always seem to show up at the exact wrong moment? Not when you're sitting at your desk trying to be brilliant — but in the shower, on a walk, right as you're drifting off to sleep.

Turns out, this isn't a you problem. It's a science problem. And once you understand what's actually happening in your brain, you can stop fighting it and start designing your day around it.
I break down the two mental modes that drive creative thinking, share three research-backed moves you can start using this week, and offer a reframe that might completely change how you think about what "real work" actually looks like.

I also sit down with my friend David Epstein — author of RANGE — who tells me a fascinating story about a Nobel Prize-winning scientist and his unusual Saturday morning ritual. Trust me, you don't want to skip that part.
And speaking of David — I actually appeared in his video too, where we dig into something counterintuitive: how boredom might be one of the most underrated drivers of innovation. Definitely worth your time.

David Epstein's video: https://youtu.be/-xjbyzc2mCk

snippet.title: The 6 Skills AI Will Never Replace
snippet.description:
What should humans do when AI can do almost everything?

AI tools can now generate text, images, code, music, and ideas at astonishing speed. If machines are getting better at producing answers, what will humans still be good for?

In this video, I walk through six human abilities that become more valuable — not less — in the age of AI:
- Asking better questions
- Developing good taste
- Iterating relentlessly
- Composing ideas into something meaningful
- Allocating human and machine talent
- Acting with integrity

These aren’t technical skills. They’re ways of thinking and behaving that help humans stay valuable, creative, and effective in a world of increasingly powerful machines.

This framework builds on ideas I began exploring more than twenty years ago in A Whole New Mind — updated for the age of AI.

When the world gets more artificial, we need to get more human.
--

snippet.title: 11 Essential Books For 2026 (Summarized In 12 Minutes)
snippet.description:
In this video, I share 11 books to read in 2026—not as a routine list, but as a response to the world we’re stepping into.

Work is evolving. Technology is accelerating. Attention is fragmented. And the skills that carried us this far may not be the ones that carry us forward. So this isn’t about reading more. It’s about reading what matters now.

Each of these books offers a way to think more clearly, make better decisions, and stay grounded while everything else speeds up. Some will challenge how you see your work. Others will sharpen how you handle change, leadership, creativity, money, or even the questions you ask yourself.

You don’t need to read all eleven. Start with one. Read it carefully. Let it stretch your thinking. And see where it leads.

**
The Work of Art – Adam Moss
Set Boundaries, Find Peace – Nedra Glover Tawwab 
The Other Side of Change – Maya Shankar
Inspire – Adam Galinsky
Strong Ground – Brené Brown
Beyond Belief – Nir Eyal  
Inside the Box – David Epstein
The Progress Principle – Teresa Amabile & Steven Kramer
Excellent Advice for Living – Kevin Kelly
Rule Breaker Investing – David Gardner
The Book of Beautiful Questions – Warren Berger

--

snippet.title: How To Fix Your Attention Span (Before It's Too Late)
snippet.description:
Subscribe to my newsletter: https://danielpink.substack.com/

In this video, I break down the growing crisis of attention fragmentation and why reclaiming your focus has never mattered more. I’ve spent years studying how we work, learn, and think, and I can tell you this: your attention isn’t broken beyond repair. But it is being pulled in more directions than ever.

I share the simple, science-backed steps I personally rely on to stay focused long enough to write seven books, even in a world built to distract us. You’ll learn how to set a true attention baseline, redesign your environment so it stops hijacking your mind, use rituals to signal your brain it’s time to work, take breaks the right way so you don’t burn out, and make a small mindset shift that helped me finish my last book when I was completely stuck.

If you’ve been feeling scattered, distracted, or constantly interrupted, this video will give you a clear, practical path to rebuild your focus one small step at a time.

And if you want more ideas on how to work smarter and live better, you can also find a link to my free newsletter, The Pink Report: https://danielpink.substack.com/

snippet.description:

Instead, I walk you through practical, brutally honest prompts—grounded in research and real-life experience—that can help you figure out what actually drives you.

snippet.title: How to Change Your Life in 90 Days
snippet.description:
You've probably tried productivity hacks that just don't stick, right? I know I have. That's why I started thinking: what if we approached our lives like scientists? In this video, I'm sharing a simple 3-step framework I use to solve any problem: Identify, Hypothesize, and Test.

I'll walk you through how to run a 90-day personal experiment to boost your willpower, productivity, and even your relationships. It’s a method I've found incredibly effective, and I want to share it with you.

Here’s what I’ll cover:
Identifying Your Problem: I'll show you how to pinpoint the areas of your life you want to improve.

Forming a Testable Hypothesis: I'll guide you in creating specific, actionable guesses about what might solve your problems.

Testing and Tracking Your Results: I'll explain how to use a "lab journal" to monitor your progress and make adjustments along the way.

Implementing a 90-Day Experiment: I'll break down how to focus on one area of your life each month for targeted improvement.

Reflecting and Refining: I'll emphasize the importance of analyzing your results to create a blueprint for future success.

I truly believe the key to lasting change is to think like a scientist: test, learn, and adapt. Let’s ditch the guesswork and use a proven method to achieve our goals.

snippet.title: How Productive People Speak
snippet.description:
Feeling stuck? Unmotivated? Like your willpower is constantly failing you? Your language might be the problem—and the solution.

In this video, I share how simple word choices can dramatically impact your motivation, decision-making, and overall performance.

Discover:
The "Don't" vs. "Can't" Switch: Why saying "I don't" instead of "I can't" creates lasting change and reinforces your identity.

snippet.title: Don't Live in the Present
snippet.description:
--
Fascinating research shows that language shapes far more than how we speak—it influences how we think about time and plan for tomorrow. 

Speakers of languages with strong present-future distinctions (like English) tend to save less and take more risks than those using languages with fuzzier time boundaries (like Mandarin). 

It's not just grammar—it's a window into how we conceive our future selves. Small linguistic differences can have profound effects on life's biggest decisions.
